headline: Steady growth as adjusted earnings pull ahead of GAAP
summary_short: Marsh McLennan's Q2 2026 revenue rose 6.2% y/y to $7.40 billion as GAAP diluted EPS reached $2.63 and adjusted EPS climbed 9% to $2.96, while the company repurchased $750 million of stock and raised its quarterly dividend 10% to $0.99 per share.
summary_long: Consulting outgrew Risk & Insurance Services, with Marsh Management Consulting revenue up 15% and Mercer up 7%, while Guy Carpenter revenue fell 2% on both a GAAP and underlying basis. Risk & Insurance Services adjusted operating income rose 3% to $1.7 billion; Consulting adjusted operating income rose 11% to $533 million. Six-month results reflect a $425 million Greensill litigation charge that cut GAAP operating income even as adjusted operating income rose 7%. The company repurchased $750 million of stock in the quarter and raised its quarterly dividend 10% to $0.99 per share, payable August 14. Cash and equivalents stood at $1.70 billion. The release stated no forward guidance for revenue or EPS.

drivers.explanation: Underlying growth was broad-based: Marsh Risk +4%, Mercer +5%, Marsh Management Consulting +13% underlying, partly offset by a 2% underlying decline at Guy Carpenter.
EPS growth tracked net income growth on a lower diluted share count from continued buybacks; adjusted EPS rose faster (+9%) after excluding noteworthy items and intangible amortization.
EBIT is a derived figure (pretax income plus interest expense) and moves with GAAP operating income and net interest cost; the release does not discuss EBIT directly.
Gross profit is computed as revenue less compensation and benefits expense; the release presents no consolidated gross-profit line, so the move mirrors revenue growth outpacing comp expense growth.
EBITDA equals EBIT plus depreciation, amortization, and identified intangible amortization; the release does not present a consolidated EBITDA figure directly.
Net income growth tracked higher operating income and adjusted income, net of tax, which excluded $130 million of noteworthy items including McGriff integration and restructuring costs.
GAAP operating income growth was held back by $130 million of noteworthy items (restructuring, McGriff integration, legal matters) versus $88 million a year earlier.
Pretax income moved with operating income, partly offset by a swing to a small investment loss versus a year-earlier gain.
Share repurchases ($1.51 billion year-to-date) and dividends paid ($878 million year-to-date) reduced equity growth despite continued net income accretion.
The buyback of 4.5 million shares for $750 million in the quarter (8.7 million shares, $1.5 billion year-to-date) reduced the diluted share count.
CEO John Doyle pointed to solid quarterly results and strong demand for Marsh's risk, people, strategy, and investments expertise across the first half.
